resources.title: ARENA 0.0 — Tensor manipulation
resources.author: ARENA / Callum McDougall
resources.target: Read Broadcasting. Use the einops and einsum examples as references when an exercise needs them.
resources.note: The local exercises are original practice tasks on the same skills; this link provides the official, broader exercise set.

resources.title: Learn the Basics
resources.author: PyTorch
resources.target: Tensors → Build Model → Autograd → Optimization. Read the relevant section when implementing that component.
resources.note: Use documentation while coding. API memorization is not a completion requirement.

resources.title: ARENA 1.1 — Transformers from scratch
resources.author: ARENA / Callum McDougall
resources.target: Inputs & Outputs, then Clean Transformer Implementation, a training run, and initial sampling. Advanced beam search and KV caching can wait.
resources.note: Open the local exercise copy with the ARENA (local GPU) kernel. Run its local setup cell first; your answers stay in this workspace.

resources.title: A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits
resources.author: Elhage et al. / Anthropic
resources.target: First pass: Transformer Overview, especially High-Level Architecture and the Residual Stream. Revisit QK/OV and two-layer composition in Module 4.
resources.note: Treat the simplifying assumptions as part of the model being studied, not properties of every transformer.

resources.title: How To Become A Mechanistic Interpretability Researcher
resources.author: Neel Nanda
resources.target: Skim the opening summary and Stage 1 now. Revisit transformer basics in Module 3; techniques/tooling in Modules 4–5; Stage 2 before a tutorial extension; Stage 3 before longer projects.
resources.depth: Brief orientation now; revisit as needed
resources.note: The one-month guideline means about 200 working hours in the post's footnote. It is not a part-time calendar deadline.

resources.title: ARENA 1.2 — TransformerLens & induction circuits
resources.author: ARENA / Callum McDougall
resources.target: Sections 1–3 first: loading and caching, finding induction heads, and hooks. Section 4 is a later deep dive.
resources.note: Open the local exercise copy with the ARENA (local GPU) kernel. Run its local setup cell first; your answers stay in this workspace.

resources.title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads
resources.author: Olsson et al. / Anthropic
resources.target: Preview the introduction and definition of induction heads. For the intervention exercise, study Argument 3 (Direct ablation) and the relevant methods.
resources.note: Distinguish evidence in small attention-only models from broader hypotheses about in-context learning.

resources.title: ARENA 1.4.1 — Indirect Object Identification
resources.author: ARENA / Callum McDougall
resources.target: Sections 1–3 for task setup, attribution, and activation patching. Sections 4–5 deepen the replication.
resources.note: Record which part you reproduced. Completing the introductory exercise is not a full paper replication.

resources.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small
resources.author: Wang et al.
resources.target: Read the task definition, the metric, and the method behind the result you select. Then inspect that result's controls and limitations.
resources.note: Choose and record the exact figure or claim before implementing the replication.

resources.title: Toy Models of Superposition
resources.author: Elhage et al. / Anthropic
resources.target: Introduction and toy setup first. Select one small configuration to reproduce if you choose the representations branch.
resources.note: A small, controlled setting for investigating what a representation stores.

resources.title: Understanding and Steering Llama 3 with Sparse Autoencoders
resources.author: Goodfire
resources.target: Read the sparse-autoencoder introduction and one steering example after studying superposition.
resources.note: Read the article as an applied example. Its old demo and API were deprecated in February 2026; this assignment does not use them.

resources.title: Under the Hood of a Reasoning Model
resources.author: Goodfire
resources.target: Preview the main examples, then choose one claim and ask what evidence would distinguish alternatives.
resources.note: A reading assignment, not a promise that a large-model replication fits the opening environment.
